title: Pay on Time
text: The captain pays the arrears before anyone asks. The men drink the captain's health.

title: Late Pay
text: The employer's runner brings apologies instead of money. Muttering runs through the ranks.

title: A Deserter from Another Company
text: At dawn a hungry soldier walks into camp. For a bowl of stew they tell who pays best around here.

title: The Sutler's Cart
text: A cart of beer and fresh bread stops by the fire. The prices are robbery, but nobody complains.

title: Snapped Bowstrings
text: Damp ruined the stock of bowstrings. The crossbowmen spend half the night saving what they can.

title: An Old Scar
text: A veteran tells the tale of Wolfenburg by the fire. The young ones listen in silence.

title: A Fight over Dice
text: A quarrel over dice ends with a broken tooth. The sergeant settles it with a bucket of cold water.

title: A Good Stretch of River
text: You find a clean place by the river. The men wash for the first time in weeks.

title: A Dead Horse
text: A baggage horse dies in the night. There will be meat, but the cart must be reloaded.

title: A Worthless Receipt
text: The council voids a supply receipt. Part of the provisions must be returned and the quartermaster curses.

title: A Grateful Reeve
text: A reeve whose people you defended this autumn sends a sack of flour and a small keg.

title: False Alarm
text: The watch sounds the alarm over a stray cow. The whole camp stands to arms for an hour.

title: An Old Debt
text: A former employer finally settles the bill through a messenger. Nobody expected it anymore.

title: Oath under the Banner
text: Some of the young ones swear the oath before the banner. The captain speaks briefly and to the point.

title: Rust and Damp
text: Rain got into the armour chests. Silver must be spent on oil and sand.

title: Rivals at the Fire
text: A patrol from another company asks for a place by the fire. The night passes in boasts and wary looks.

title: A Priest of Sigmar
text: A wandering priest holds a service before a battle that has not yet come. The men sleep easier.

title: A Sick Camp
text: Bad water doubles over half the camp. Nobody feels like drilling in the morning.

title: An Abandoned Wagon
text: An abandoned cart stands on a side road. Someone fled in haste and left provisions.

title: News of War
text: The road brings word of musters in the east. A good soldier will soon be expensive.

title: A Drunken Corporal
text: A corporal wakes the camp with a song about a miller's three daughters and ends up in the slop pit.

title: A Broken Bridge
text: A flood took the bridge on your route. The detour costs a day and a few rations.

title: A Reward from the Town
text: The council sends a token purse for good order during your last stay.

title: A Grave by the Road
text: By the road lie bodies in the colours of your old company. You bury them without a word.

title: A Winter Contract
text: A nearby town council asks whether the company would take service over the winter. Secure quarters cheer everyone.

title: Spoiled Bolts
text: Someone left a crate of bolts in the rain. Half have warped and are good only for kindling.

title: A Matter of Honour
text: Two soldiers want to fight over an insult to someone's mother. The captain allows fists, not steel.

title: New Boots
text: The quartermaster buys a crate of boots at a bargain. For the first time in months nobody complains of blisters.

title: The Elector's Recruiter
text: A recruiter promises Elector's pay to anyone who leaves the company. Nobody goes, but everyone thinks about it.

title: Hunting Hares
text: A free evening ends with a hunt. A few hares and a partridge go into the pot.

title: Camp Fever
text: Several men have chills and the flux. The barber-surgeon orders the water boiled, but the day is lost.

title: A Veteran Leaves
text: The oldest soldier announces a return to their home village. The company sees them off with a round on the captain.

title: Praise from the Employer
text: The employer sends a letter of thanks. The captain reads it aloud by the fire.

title: A Thief in the Baggage
text: Someone gets into the supply cart at night. By morning two sacks are missing.

title: A Roadside Smith
text: A travelling smith sharpens the whole company's weapons for a fair price.

title: News from the Border
text: A passing merchant speaks of war on the border. The mercenaries are already counting future pay.

title: Mutiny at the Stewpot
text: Some of the men refuse duty until they get full rations.
okText: The sergeant forms them up and ends it without a single blow.

title: Green Recruits Panic
text: A noise in the woods sends the new recruits into a panic.
okText: The sergeant calmly musters the squad and has them count their bolts.

title: A Charge on the Baggage
text: A group of riders tries to break the carts on the edge of camp.
okText: The halberdiers close the gap and the riders turn away.

title: A Show for the Townsfolk
text: Curious locals come to look at the camp and mock the soldiers.
okText: The halberdier does something with the polearm that has the townsfolk tossing coins.

title: Wolves at the Stores
text: Something circles the camp and gets at the sacks of food.
okText: The crossbowman waits still until dawn, and the first bolt settles it.

title: A Shooting Wager
text: Soldiers from another company propose a wager on marksmanship.
okText: The crossbowman hits a coin on a stake and the wager stays with the company.

title: A Torn Banner
text: The wind has torn the company's colours. The men take it as an ill omen.
okText: The standard bearer stitches the cloth by the fire and raises it higher than before.

title: Company Day
text: It is the anniversary of the company's founding, but nobody feels like celebrating.
okText: The standard bearer brings out the banner and reminds everyone why they are here.

title: Fever in the Tent
text: A wound from the last skirmish festers. The patient raves all night.
okText: The barber-surgeon opens the wound, cauterises it and the fever breaks by morning.

title: A Birth in the Village
text: Peasants beg for help with a difficult birth.
okText: The barber-surgeon goes with them and returns at dawn with a basket of food.

title: A Discrepancy in the Ledger
text: The number of sacks does not match the ledger.
okText: The quartermaster traces the shortfall to the supplier and forces a refund.

title: A Bargain at Market
text: A merchant is selling off salted pork at a suspiciously good price.
okText: The quartermaster checks the barrels and takes only the good ones.
